remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
The negative AI jobs outcome just continues to not be happening as some predicted. A large portion of enterprises I talk with -across industries- are still hiring, just with a tilt in the kind of roles they’re going after.

They’re finding that AI is letting them do more, and Jevons paradox is actually playing out. They’re hiring engineers to go after problems they couldn’t tackle before. They’re hiring in sales because they can go deeper in client relationships now with the help of AI. They’re hiring in internal FDEs to help them deploy AI. And so on.

Anyone using AI merely to cut costs eventually just gets outcompeted by companies that use AI to better serve their customers and drive more breakthroughs in their business. 

Could this trend change at some point? Sure. But for now this appears to be the trajectory we’re on.
remarks.translation: 一些人曾预测AI会导致大量失业，但这种情况至今仍未发生。我与各行业众多企业交流时发现，它们仍在持续招聘，只是岗位类型有所侧重。这些企业发现AI让它们能完成更多工作，杰文斯悖论正在现实中上演。它们正在招聘工程师，去攻克以往无法解决的问题；借助AI深化客户关系，销售岗位也在扩招；同时招募内部现场部署工程师来推进AI落地，诸如此类。那些仅将AI用于削减成本的企业，最终会被利用AI优化客户服务、推动业务突破的竞争对手超越。这种趋势未来会改变吗？当然有可能。但就目前而言，这似乎正是我们正处的发展轨迹。

remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
Kimi's paper underlines the importance of the right security boundary for agents to run in.

tl:DR: container-level isolation is not enough. In their experiments, agents crashed the underlying machine (via kernel panics).

Firecracker microVMs (as in Vercel Sandbox) are safe. https://t.co/wvbdBo5Ng8 https://t.co/OFCWYaiKw7
remarks.translation: Kimi的论文强调了为智能体设定正确安全边界的重要性。简而言之：容器级别的隔离是不够的。在他们的实验中，智能体导致底层机器崩溃（通过内核恐慌）。Firecracker微虚拟机（如Vercel沙箱中的）是安全的。https://t.co/wvbdBo5Ng8 https://t.co/OFCWYaiKw7

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
Most product review meetings are annoying because they’re poorly run.

The best product reviews compress months of learnings into an hour by simulating the market reaction to your ideas. 

That only works if the people in the room deeply understand the space, have great product sense, strong opinions, and are often right.

Too many product reviews have drifted toward status updates, leadership visibility, and cross-functional alignment.

When that happens, people naturally resent them because it feels more like overhead and less like learning.
remarks.translation: 大多数产品评审会议之所以令人厌烦，是因为组织得一团糟。优秀的产品评审能将数月的经验浓缩成一小时的讨论，通过模拟市场对你创意的反应来实现价值。但这只有在与会者深刻理解行业、具备敏锐产品直觉、持有鲜明观点且判断准确率较高时才能奏效。如今太多产品评审已偏离正轨，沦为进度汇报、领导刷存在感和跨部门协调会。当这种情况发生时，人们自然会心生抵触——因为感觉更像是额外负担，而非学习机会。

podcasts.originalTitle: Factory's Matan Grinberg: The Coming ‘Dark Factory’ Where Software Builds Itself
podcasts.excerpt: 工厂于2023年4月开始打造全自主编程智能体，比企业真正准备好早了整整两年。马坦·格林伯格如今坦言，这无异于判断失误。这位Factory联合创始人兼CEO讲述了公司如何熬过那段"沙漠跋涉期"，包括在产品未能让开发者痴迷时，毅然将几乎全部收入返还给客户。马坦提出了一个反常规的技术观点：模型无关的集成框架，优于OpenAI和Anthropic等实验室偏好的模型与框架协同设计，因为让集成框架接触多种模型，能避免其过度适配任何单一模型。他认为，像GLM这样的开放权重模型，只需保持比前沿技术落后一代，就能以极低的成本占据大部分token使用量；而CIO们很快会像评估人力投入一样，为每个新增token的使用找到合理依据。展望未来，他预测90%的编程工作将……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Factory started building fully autonomous coding agents in April 2023, two years before enterprises were ready. Matan Grinberg now says this is indistinguishable from being wrong. The Factory co-founder and CEO explains how the company survived its "journey in the desert," including the decision to hand nearly all of its revenue back to customers when the product wasn't making developers obsessed. Matan makes the contrarian technical case that a model-agnostic harness beats the model-and-harness co-design that labs like OpenAI and Anthropic favor, because exposing a harness to many models keeps it from overfitting to any single one. He argues open-weight models like GLM will capture the majority of tokens by staying one generation behind the frontier at a fraction of the cost, and that CIOs will soon justify every incremental token the way they justify headcount. podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第90集：人工智能先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 尤尔根·施密德胡伯博士，这位享誉全球的科学家与人工智能研究者，被公认为该领域的先驱之一。他通过其实验室的工作，孕育了当今Transformer架构、长短期记忆网络（LSTM）以及递归自我改进等关键理念。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件瓶颈；随着开源技术紧追封闭实验室的步伐，当前对AI数据中心的投资热潮即将迎来修正；而通往通用智能的路径，在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非依赖互联网数据。在结尾部分，他重新审视了主流AI安全论点，并描绘了一幅宏大愿景：自我复制的机器人社会终将殖民整个太阳系。 (0:00) 引言 (1:24) 超人类AI还有多远？ (2:27) ChatGPT为何未令他惊讶 (3:21) 递归自我改进之路 (9:01) AI会迎来爆发式飞跃吗…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. (0:00) Intro (1:24) How Close Is Superhuman AI? (2:27) Why ChatGPT Didn't Surprise Him (3:21) The Path to Recursive Self-Improvement (9:01) Will AI Takeoff…

podcasts.originalTitle: Building an Autonomous Delivery Experience with DoorDash Co-Founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang
podcasts.excerpt: DoorDash 不仅仅是一家配送公司。从创立之初，联合创始人 Andy Fang 和 Stanley Tang 就将其作为一家机器人与自动驾驶公司来运营。Andy 和 Stanley 与 Sarah Guo 一起探讨了自动驾驶技术和人工智能如何重塑消费习惯、商业和配送。他们谈到了 Ask DoorDash 的推出，这是一个自然语言界面，既能推动餐厅发现，也能促进更大额的杂货订单。他们还讨论了 Dot，这是他们自主研发的自动驾驶配送机器人，已在凤凰城运营超过两年，并展示了他们在自动驾驶技术中面临并解决的运营和硬件挑战。Andy 和 Stanley 还谈到了自动驾驶配送中的“首尾 100 英尺问题”，为什么多模式策略是成功的关键，如何扩展自动驾驶和运营规模，以及为什么他们相信未来 DoorDash 需要更多而非更少的 Dasher。立即注册…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: DoorDash is not just a delivery company. From its inception, co-founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang operated it as a robotics and autonomy company. Andy and Stanley join Sarah Guo to explain how autonomous tech and AI are reshaping consumer habits, commerce, and delivery. Andy and Stanley talk about the rollout of Ask DoorDash, a natural-language interface that’s driving both restaurant discovery and larger grocery orders. They also discuss Dot, their in-house autonomous delivery robot that has operated in Phoenix for over two years, and how it highlights the operational and hardware challenges they have faced and solved in autonomous tech.
